description: SqlStatementNormalizer.normalize(input, system) must return expected (null: nothing exported). Shared by every LogDrop tracing implementation; the Java core is the reference.

cases.name: number and string literals
cases.input: SELECT name FROM orders WHERE id = 42 AND secret <> 'sql-secret'
cases.expected: SELECT name FROM orders WHERE id = ? AND secret <> ?

cases.name: signed exponent and escaped quote
cases.input: UPDATE card_holder SET balance = -12.5e3, note = 'it''s mine' WHERE id = 7
cases.expected: UPDATE card_holder SET balance = ?, note = ? WHERE id = ?

cases.name: identifiers with digits, booleans and hex
cases.input: SELECT * FROM t1_0 JOIN v2_items ON t1_0.id = v2_items.order_id WHERE flag = TRUE AND data = 0xCAFE
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM t1_0 JOIN v2_items ON t1_0.id = v2_items.order_id WHERE flag = ? AND data = ?

cases.name: bind placeholders are kept
cases.input: SELECT * FROM a WHERE x = ? AND y = $1 AND z = :name AND w = @p1 AND v = ?2
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM a WHERE x = ? AND y = $1 AND z = :name AND w = @p1 AND v = ?2

cases.name: IN list of one
cases.input: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (1)
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (?)

cases.name: IN list of three
cases.input: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (1, 2,3)
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (?)

cases.name: multi-row VALUES and trailing semicolon
cases.input:
INSERT INTO items (a, b) VALUES (1, 'x'), (2, 'y'),
 (3, 'z');
cases.expected: INSERT INTO items (a, b) VALUES (?, ?)

cases.name: block and line comments
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = ?

cases.name: comment marker inside a string
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = 'it''s -- not a comment'
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = ?

cases.name: dollar-quoted string
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = $tag$ secret value $tag$
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = ?

cases.name: string cut off by a length limit
cases.input: SELECT * FROM t WHERE email = 'person@exam
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM t WHERE email = ?

cases.name: block comment cut off by a length limit
cases.input: SELECT * FROM t /* user ahmet
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM t

cases.name: double quotes are identifiers in PostgreSQL
cases.input: SELECT "Id" FROM "Orders" WHERE "Name" = 'x'
cases.expected: SELECT "Id" FROM "Orders" WHERE "Name" = ?

cases.name: double quotes are strings in MySQL
cases.input: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE name = "person@example.com"
cases.expected: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE name = ?

cases.name: double quotes are strings in MariaDB, system name case-insensitive
cases.input: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE name = "person@example.com"
cases.expected: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE name = ?

cases.name: hash is an identifier in SQL Server
cases.input: SELECT * FROM #orders WHERE id = 5
cases.expected: SELECT * FROM #orders WHERE id = ?

cases.name: hash starts a comment in MySQL
cases.input:
SELECT a FROM b # user ahmet
WHERE c = 5
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = ?

cases.name: subtraction keeps its operand, a negative literal is masked
cases.input: SELECT total-1 FROM t WHERE x = -1
cases.expected: SELECT total-? FROM t WHERE x = ?

cases.name: no system still masks
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = 'x' AND d = 1
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = ? AND d = ?

cases.name: hex string literal: the quoted part is masked as a string first, the X prefix stays
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = X'0aff'
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c = X?

cases.name: decimal and exponent forms
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c > 1.5 AND d < 2e10 AND e = 3E-2
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c > ? AND d < ? AND e = ?

cases.name: IN list with strings and newlines
cases.input:
SELECT a FROM b WHERE c IN (
'a',
'b'
)
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c IN (?)

cases.name: lower-case keywords keep their case
cases.input: select a from b where c in (1,2) and d = true
cases.expected: select a from b where c IN (?) and d = ?

cases.name: several trailing semicolons
cases.input: DELETE FROM b WHERE c = 1 ; ;
cases.expected: DELETE FROM b WHERE c = ?

cases.name: multi-line block comment
cases.input:
SELECT a /* line one
line two 'x' */ FROM b
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b

cases.name: line comment at the end
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b -- card 4111111111111111
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b

cases.name: Turkish text in a string
cases.input: SELECT a FROM müşteri WHERE ad = 'Çağrı Öztürk'
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM müşteri WHERE ad = ?

cases.name: parameter placeholders in VALUES rows
cases.input: INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (?), (?), (?)
cases.expected: INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (?)

cases.name: number inside an identifier with a dollar
cases.input: SELECT col$1 FROM b WHERE c = 2
cases.expected: SELECT col$1 FROM b WHERE c = ?

cases.name: number after a closing parenthesis keeps
cases.input: SELECT (a)1 FROM b
cases.expected: SELECT (a)1 FROM b

cases.name: only ASCII whitespace collapses (a no-break space stays)
cases.input: SELECT a  FROM b
cases.expected: SELECT a  FROM b

cases.name: trimming removes control characters
cases.input: SELECT 1
cases.expected: SELECT ?

cases.name: trimming keeps a leading no-break space
cases.input: SELECT 1
cases.expected: SELECT ?

cases.name: an IN list after a no-break space does not collapse
cases.input: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c IN (1, 2)
cases.expected: SELECT a FROM b WHERE c IN (?, ?)

cases.name: digits after a non-ASCII letter are masked
cases.input: SELECT ş1 FROM b
cases.expected: SELECT ş? FROM b
